principles: Production behavior is correct and must not change; only tests/config may change.
Never weaken an assertion to make a test pass — fix the test environment, not the expectation.
A smoke must be hermetic: its result must not depend on ambient on-disk files at the cwd.
Keep timeout ceilings finite so a true hang still surfaces.
drivers: test:all must be trustworthy (green) again so the suite gate has signal.
Two authority smokes pass/fail depending on whether an authority_trust.env exists at cwd — a flakiness source.
The original triage misdiagnosed autopilot-authority as stale-assertion; the empirical repro shows it is non-hermetic.

options.name: A-fileReader-hermetic
pros: 0 production change — fileReader is an existing test seam (options.fileReader ?? defaultAuthorityFileReader).
Keeps every assertion intact incl. shadow.status===warn — no coverage loss.
Makes result independent of cwd; passes with or without a planted authority_trust.env.
Same mechanism for both autopilot and multi-host — consistent.
cons: Must thread fileReader through every env-only call site (~14 in multi-host, the buildAuthorityStatus path in autopilot) — easy to miss one.
Slightly more verbose test call sites.

options.name: B-weaken-assertion
cons: FACTUALLY WRONG: production keeps shadow no-URL behavior, so this breaks the smoke from a clean cwd / CI.
Weakens a valid assertion and hides a real URL-empty warning — violates the no-weakening principle.

options.name: C-env-gate-skip
cons: Loses coverage of off-by-default machinery that CAN and should run in-process.
Masks the real non-hermeticity bug instead of fixing it.

options.name: D-cwd-redirect
pros: Also avoids reading the dev authority_trust.env.
cons: Brittle — relies on process.chdir or passing cwd everywhere; other code may still read process.cwd().
fileReader override is the purpose-built test seam and is more explicit/localized.

rationale: Option A uses the purpose-built fileReader test seam to make the smokes hermetic with 0 production change and 0 assertion weakening, and is verifiable by running each smoke from a cwd containing a planted authority_trust.env (must still pass). B is factually wrong and breaks CI; C loses coverage; D is more brittle than the dedicated seam.

preMortem.scenario: Implementer misses one env-only call site in multi-host (~14 sites), so the smoke still leaks the dev authority_trust.env at one assertion.
preMortem.trigger: Smoke passes from clean cwd but still FAILS from a cwd with a planted authority_trust.env.
preMortem.consequence: False sense of done; test:all still flaky depending on whether the runner cwd has the file.
preMortem.mitigation: Verification requires running each smoke from a planted-authority_trust.env cwd (mktemp + write LATTICE_AUTHORITY_LIVE_URL) and asserting exit 0 — not just from /tmp. grep the smoke for any resolveAuthorityVerdictBacking/loadAuthorityConfig/buildAuthorityStatus call lacking fileReader.

preMortem.scenario: Implementer accidentally edits production source (authority-client.ts / authority-mode.ts) to thread fileReader, instead of only the smoke files.
preMortem.trigger: git diff main...HEAD --stat shows a non-test file changed.
preMortem.consequence: Violates the 0-production-change constraint and execution boundary; could change real behavior.
preMortem.mitigation: fileReader is ALREADY an existing production parameter — no production edit is needed. Execution boundary allows only the 4 test/config files. REVIEW + delivery reviewer check git diff --stat is test-only.

preMortem.scenario: Implementer weakens the autopilot assertion (warn->pass) per the stale triage text in some cached prompt.
preMortem.trigger: shadow.status assertion changed to pass or readinessWarnings===0 in the diff.
preMortem.consequence: Smoke breaks from a clean cwd / CI; a valid no-URL warning is hidden; production-correctness regression masked.
preMortem.mitigation: CHK-001 context, description, and background all explicitly forbid this; implementer prompt restates KEEP shadow.status===warn; reviewer greps the diff for assertion changes.

preMortem.scenario: A timeout value is raised to an absurd/infinite ceiling while re-verifying CHK-002.
preMortem.trigger: smoke-manifest.json shows a timeoutMs like 0/Infinity/huge value.
preMortem.consequence: A future real hang would never TIMEOUT, silently stalling the suite.
preMortem.mitigation: Constraint: finite measured ceiling only; re-verify keeps existing 180000-240000 values unless a measured standalone time needs more, and never sets Infinity.
